od_walker.text: All hundred and seventy-seven miles. Chepstow to Prestatyn, or the other way round, if you like going down hills.
You cross the border more than twenty times on the Path. The border doesn't seem to mind.

od_bargee.text: Across Pontcysyllte at four miles an hour. Thirty-eight metres up. I don't look down. My wife does it for me, and describes it.
Telford built it in iron and stone. The mortar was lime and ox blood, they say. Nobody likes to think about the ox blood, but it's still holding up.

od_singer.text: The International Eisteddfod began in 1947. Choirs from all over the world came to sing in a tent in a Welsh field, just two years after the war. People thought it a very odd idea. It's been going ever since.
Every July the town fills up with folk dancers and the smell of chip fat. Lovely.

od_railman.text: The Welshpool and Llanfair is a narrow gauge line, two foot six, opened in 1903. It was nearly lost in the sixties, and a lot of enthusiasts saved it with sandwiches and shovels.
It runs through the border country at a walking pace. It's the only way to see the Dyke without getting your boots dirty.
